question: The Maski Ashoka Inscription is situated in which state of India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Karnataka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Maski Ashoka Inscription is located in **Maski village** of Raichur district in the state of **Karnataka, India**.
 
• This inscription is significant as it was the first to explicitly mention the name **Ashoka**, identifying him with the title "Devanampiya Piyadasi" (Beloved of the Gods).
 
• The Maski inscription was discovered by **C. Beadon** in 1915, and it played a crucial role in confirming the identity of Ashoka as the ruler responsible for the edicts.
 
• It is one of the **Minor Rock Edicts** of Ashoka and promotes the principles of Dhamma (righteousness).
 
• The inscription is written in the **Prakrit language** using the Brahmi script, which was widely used during the Mauryan period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ashoka and His Edicts:**

 
 
• Ashoka, the Mauryan emperor, ruled during the 3rd century BCE and is renowned for his promotion of Buddhism and Dhamma (moral conduct).
 
• His inscriptions, known as **Ashokan Edicts**, are spread across the Indian subcontinent and are categorized into Major Rock Edicts, Minor Rock Edicts, Pillar Edicts, and Cave Inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Maski Inscription:**
 
 
• Before the Maski discovery, it was unclear whether "Devanampiya Piyadasi" referred to Ashoka or another ruler.
 
• The Maski edict confirmed that "Devanampiya Piyadasi" was indeed **Ashoka**, solidifying his connection with the inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Prakrit and Brahmi:**
 
 
• **Prakrit** was the common language of the people during the Mauryan period, used in many of Ashoka's edicts.
 
• **Brahmi script** is one of the oldest writing systems in India, serving as the precursor to many modern Indian scripts.
 
 
 
• **Raichur District:**
 
 
• Raichur is located in northern Karnataka and is historically significant due to its association with several ancient kingdoms, including the Mauryas.
 
• It is home to many archaeological and historical sites, including the Maski inscription.
